title: Corpus span label
description: One line of a labels.jsonl file. A label says what the correct linter/AI output is for a span of text (violation), or that a span must not be flagged (clean, exempt), or that a block is fully labelled (block-complete). See docs/testing/CORPUS.md.

id.description: <project>/<name>, unique across the corpus. The part before the slash is the project used for per-project scores.

file.description: Topic or snippet path relative to the project root, forward slashes.

block.description: Absolute path of qualified element names with 1-based same-name sibling indexes (always present except on html, head and body): /html/body/ol[1]/li[3]/p[1]. A block is a text-owning element (h1-h6, p, li, td, th, dt, dd, caption, figcaption, blockquote, pre, div, MadCap:dropDownHead, MadCap:toggler); its plain text excludes nested blocks. Without quote, any element (img, table) may be named and the label covers all of it.

quote.description: Selected text, exactly as in the block's plain text.

prefix.description: Up to 24 characters of block text before the quote; disambiguates repeated quotes.

suffix.description: Up to 24 characters of block text after the quote.

label.description: violation: a finding is expected. clean: no finding from `rules` may touch the span. exempt: a rule would match but the text is fine here (UI label, quoted text, code, boilerplate); counts as clean for `rules`. ambiguous: excluded from scoring. block-complete: every problem a lint rule can find in this block is labelled; any other finding in it is a false positive.

kind.description: Defect taxonomy id from defects.yaml; required for violations. Independent of rule ids.

rules.description: Acceptable rule ids (google:word-list/221), families (google:word-list/*), layers (google:*), * (any), lint (any non-AI finding), ai (any AI finding) or ai:<kind> (an AI finding of that judgment kind). For clean/exempt: the rules that must not fire there.

fix.description: The corrected text, when the label has one.

reason.description: Why a span is clean or exempt (required for those).

context.description: Same vocabulary as TextLine/Segment context in the engine (issue #53). Computed from the DOM by the corpus tools, not by Core.

origin.description: seeded: injected by a generator. natural: present in the source text.

seed.description: Generator, variant and any source ids for seeded labels.

status.description: Only verified labels are scored; proposed and disputed ones count as ambiguous.

by.description: Sources that agreed: generator, llm-a, llm-b, human, hand-read, ...

split.description: Chosen by file, fixed per project.
